QEVA RECOVERY CORE 0.5
======================

PURPOSE
QEVA preserves explicit mathematical objects, executable mechanisms, scoped
evidence, provenance, history, and source records. This is a low-complexity
recovery description. The domain, website, database, and present institution
are replaceable.

EVIDENCE DOMAINS
1. LOGICAL: exact definitions, axioms, statements, conjectures, proofs,
   counterexamples, algorithms, frameworks, and typed relations.
2. HISTORICAL: works, people, traditions, dates, transmission, correction,
   independent discovery, uncertainty, and dispute.
3. CORPUS: provider identifiers, retrieval events, raw-byte fixity, rights,
   normalized works, citations, and source-located extraction candidates.
4. QUALIFICATION: append-only reviews, replays, refutations, replications, and
   certificates bound to exact subjects, methods, actors, dates, and artifacts.
5. VIEWS: HTML, maps, plots, search, catalogs, and other replaceable software.

PERMANENT SEPARATIONS
  syntax            is not semantics
  derivation        is not model-independent truth
  citation          is not logical dependence
  co-occurrence     is not mechanism
  analogy           is not equivalence
  simulation        is not proof
  extraction        is not qualification
  publication       is not truth
  accessibility     is not redistribution permission

FOUNDATIONAL STANCE
QEVA does not claim that all mathematics has one uncontested absolute root.
It records explicit languages, rules, models, and interpretations. Classical
set-theoretic, constructive/type-theoretic, categorical, and other foundations
may coexist. A bridge must name the translation or interpretation supporting it.

IDENTITY AND REVISION
  qeva:1:sequence@2                    exact logical object
  qeva-experiment:1:collatz-orbit@1    exact experiment
  qeva-analyzer:1:cycle-detector@1     exact analyzer contract

The namespace number is part of identity, not a release number. Released bytes
never change. Later revisions form contiguous supersedes chains. Current streams
contain exactly one numeric-latest revision per stable ID; all streams preserve
every revision. A readable ID aids citation; a digest detects content change.
Neither proves authorship or mathematical truth.

OBJECTS, EXPERIMENTS, AND OBSERVATIONS
Object fields are described by qeva-object.schema.json. Experiment 0.1 records
name a bounded engine kernel, numeric semantics, parameters, randomness,
observer, analyzers, resource limits, provenance, and exact engine artifact
SHA-256. No experiment executes user-supplied code.

A run conforming to run.schema.json records normalized parameters, result, completion, stopped_reason,
states_emitted, operations_used, and run_sha256. The run hash covers the exact
experiment, declared engine artifact digest, parameters, and result. The engine
cannot attest its own bytes from a caller-supplied record; mirrors must compare
the declaration with the shipped file before claiming replay. An observation names
its exact subject, run (or null for aggregate attacks), analyzer revision, exact
analyzer artifact SHA-256, evidence class, finite claim scope, method, result,
and proof status. Partial output never becomes proof.

validateRun checks structure, bounds, digests, and analyzer contracts. It does
not establish analyzer truth. Before attributing a run or observation to the
official implementation, validateRunAgainstExperiment must replay the named
kernel and require canonical equality. analyzeRun performs that semantic replay
before producing an official observation. Schema conformance alone is not
execution provenance.

PROOF AND TRUTH
  Gamma |-_{S} P   means a permitted finite S-derivation of P from Gamma.
  M |= P           means P is satisfied in model M under declared semantics.

Neither has a complete meaning until the language, S or M, assumptions, and
interpretation are recoverable. Strong qualifications bind the exact subject
canonical digest, statement text/hash, dependency digests, certificate bytes,
checker bytes, rule set, and environment.

RELATIONS
Logical, pedagogical, computational, historical, and citation edges remain
different types. The inherited dependency field lacked formal proof roles, so
QEVA 0.5 publishes migrated edges as CANDIDATE. A qualification may later
promote an exact edge. Visualization direction is never semantic direction.

ENCODING AND CANONICALIZATION
Text is UTF-8 without BOM; generated lines end LF (0x0A). JSON follows RFC 8259
and must not contain duplicate member names, lone Unicode surrogates, sparse
arrays, non-plain values, NaN, or infinities. Canonical JSON emits Unicode
directly, sorts object names by UTF-16 code units, preserves array order, uses
ECMAScript shortest finite-number serialization, has no insignificant
whitespace, and appends one LF. Integer-valued numbers outside
[-(2^53-1), 2^53-1] are forbidden; larger exact integers are decimal strings.
JSONL contains one canonical record per line.

NUMERIC BOUNDARY
Integer kernels use exact BigInt values serialized as decimal strings. Binary64
kernels pin operation order and engine bytes. QEVA 0.5 signal/optimization
examples use host Math.sin/Math.exp; their hashes are regression evidence for
the pinned implementation, not a claim of cross-engine transcendental identity.
timeout_ms is declarative; synchronous v0.5 enforces state/operation bounds and
does not claim timer preemption.

FIXITY AND AUTHENTICITY
SHA-256 and SHA-512 manifests provide present-day byte fixity. They do not prove
authorship, truth, provenance, or timeless security, and both are SHA-2. Future
releases must add algorithm agility and multi-party signatures while retaining
the old bytes and manifests.

RECOVERY ORDER
1. Verify outer MANIFEST.sha256 and/or MANIFEST.sha512.
2. Read RELEASE.json, README.md, and this CORE.txt.
3. Read archive/CATALOG.tsv, archive/current.jsonl, then archive/all.jsonl.
4. Read experiments/current.jsonl and analyzers/current.jsonl; consult their
   all.jsonl streams for history.
5. Read archive/qualifications/index.jsonl and the named artifacts/checkers.
6. Read corpus/source-registry.json and rights records before third-party data.
7. Verify snapshot/QEVA-BAG tag and payload manifests. Its payload is data-only;
   regenerate views rather than trusting partial archived HTML.
8. For the complete outer release only, run from its site root:
     python3 -B scripts/verify.py
     python3 -B scripts/verify_runtime.py
     python3 -B scripts/verify_preservation.py
     node scripts/test_engine.mjs
     python3 -B scripts/test_harvester.py
9. The QEVA-BAG payload is deliberately data-and-engine only; it cannot verify
   or recreate the full presentation layer. From QEVA-BAG/data run only:
     python3 -B scripts/verify.py --tier a
     node scripts/test_engine.mjs
   Read BAG-RECOVERY.txt before attempting a migration.

MIRRORS AND SUCCESSION
Anyone may mirror QEVA-native material. A migration preserves source bytes,
writes a new representation, documents the transformation, and keeps both.
A successor may continue from a complete mirror but must not impersonate an
earlier release. Long survival requires independent custody, repeated recovery,
media/cryptography migration, transparent governance, and the right to fork.

END QEVA RECOVERY CORE 0.5
